A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Alignment across Trees. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, generalization and ablation results on four datasets, together with representation and attention visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original sensitivity, approximation-error, labeling, class-imbalance and efficiency experiments.

M1.justification: The main feature-extraction, manifold-alignment and optimization procedure remains intact. Appendix C.12 adds the sample-reweighted Ours-balanced training variant as a preliminary adaptation, without replacing the primary method.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR100, SUN, ImageNet and Rare Species for few-shot and base/novel/whole taxonomic classification. Additional backbone, labeling and diagnostic experiments remain within this coverage; the artifact visualizations use already-covered ImageNet classes.

E2.justification: The existing MaPLe, PromptSRC, ProTeCt, MERU and HyCoCLIP comparisons remain. v2 adds squared, squared-log and squared-reciprocal curvature-distance controls in Table 8, and adds ProTeCt to attention-map comparisons that previously showed only the proposed method.

E3.justification: The original training and evaluation settings are retained. New protocols include ViT-L/14 evaluation, hyperparameter sweeps, three clustering-quality metrics, alternative species-label preprocessing, approximation checks using one million vector pairs, and efficiency measurements over 1,000 batches with specified training/inference batch sizes.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations, v2 tests alternative manifold distances, removal of cross-attention, layer/curvature/loss-weight sensitivity, approximation and r-estimation errors, label-concatenation dependence and sample reweighting. It also adds quantitative clustering analysis, artifact attention comparisons, learned-curvature analysis and computational profiling.

E5.justification: Both versions report LA, HCA and MTA averaged over three independent runs in Appendix B.4. Neither reports seed identities, dispersion estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new approximation-error diagnostics do not introduce uncertainty reporting for repeated experimental runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for the new controls and analyses, including a 5.3% mean Taylor-approximation error and measured computational overhead. Original Table 1 remains numerically unchanged, but some retained harmonic means change: CIFAR100 MaPLe+ProTeCt LA changes from 78.29 to 78.40 in v1 Table 3 versus v2 Table 5.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the c2 update in Equation 18, makes the implicit derivatives in Equation 20 explicit, and states that the proposed distance lacks symmetry and the triangle inequality. The central theorem, propositions and Appendix A proof arguments remain substantially unchanged; Appendix D supplies conceptual justification rather than new formal proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contribution list and main conclusion retain the same claims about hierarchical feature construction, heterogeneous manifold alignment, existence and uniqueness of the intermediate optimum, and classification advantages. Additional evidence does not redefine these central contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning single-curvature expressiveness, domain shifts, class imbalance and the non-metric distance. Appendix D introduces information-bottleneck and attention-smoothing explanations and an anti-collapse argument, while new analyses support interpretations about approximation robustness, curvature differences and computational costs.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents batchwise estimation of r, weighting coefficients for the no-attention control, alternative label construction and profiling settings. Existing training details remain largely unchanged. The front-page resource link changes from a repository to a project page, without establishing a change in actual code availability.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against relative-representation communication, CNN taxonomy classification, latent-hierarchy research and biological vision-language models, including BioCLIP2 and Biotrove. Appendix D adds literature-based distinctions concerning attention suppression and feature fusion. These are substantive positioning additions, not merely bibliography updates.

P1.justification: The main narrative and most retained exposition remain recognizable. v2 corrects language and terminology, updates author and conference information, adds acknowledgements, relocates the hyperbolic comparison, and reorganizes appendix topics. Most expansion consists of additional scientific content rather than extensive rewriting of existing prose.

P2.justification: v2 adds numerous diagnostic tables and approximation-error, efficiency and artifact-attention figures. Figure 6 becomes a baseline-versus-method comparison, while earlier animal visualizations are retained in the appendix. The full generalization table moves to the appendix with a shorter main-text display, and the hyperbolic comparison is relocated.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the central design choices through direct distance and cross-attention controls, approximation checks, sensitivity tests and alternative-label experiments, addressing important gaps in v1's supporting evidence. Computational profiling and explicit limitations also make applicability easier to assess. The remaining SUN baseline inconsistency between Tables 5 and 7 tempers these gains but does not outweigh the substantial improvement in evidential support and transparency.
